note: Two books to digitize next, chosen by the owner to replace the old collections.paperlanterns.ink subdomain. Entries follow the item shape of config/wishlist.json; merge them into its `items` once that file is committed, then delete this file. Nothing has been extracted or spent on either book.

items.title: Glimpses of Bengal: Selected from the Letters of Sir Rabindranath Tagore, 1885 to 1895
items.correspondents: Rabindranath Tagore to his niece Indira Devi; translator to be taken from the title page or preface
items.rights: Public domain: published 1921 (US public domain); Tagore died 1941, so public domain in India since 2002. The Archive marks this copy NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
items.pg_status: On Project Gutenberg (ebook 7951), an exception to the wishlist's anti-duplication rule: the owner wants it on the site because the old subdomain carried 67 of its letters, and Gutenberg has no page-by-page scan alignment.
items.why_this_edition: The 1921 Macmillan first edition, scanned at 400 ppi with lossless JP2 by a research library (UC), which the wishlist prefers over DLI scans. The old subdomain mislabelled this book as 'The Letters of Sir Rabindranath Tagore (1921)' and gave its letters invented titles; ignore those.
items.pitch: A young Tagore's letters from the family estates on the Padma: river life, villagers, monsoon and the making of a poet.

items.title: Letters from a Father to His Daughter: Being a Brief Account of the Early Days of the World, Written for Children
items.correspondents: Jawaharlal Nehru to his daughter Indira
items.source_library: Digital Library of India (scanned at S.V. Digital Library, Tirupati, from SNL Vetapalem)
items.rights: Public domain: published 1929, so US public domain since 2025; Nehru died 1964, so public domain in India since 1 January 2025 (life plus 60 years).
items.why_this_edition: The first edition: its text layer shows the 1929 title page and contents (foreword, 31 letters, illustrations including a Sphinx frontispiece and fossils). The 1931 second edition (rkas.245.lettersfromfathe0000jawa, used by the old subdomain) stays in US copyright until 1 January 2027, and ims0594-lettersfromafathertohisdaughter-1929 names Geoffrey Cumberlege, OUP's publisher from 1945, so it is a later reprint mislabelled 1929. This is a DLI scan, which the wishlist usually avoids: run triage-pdf first, and if it is bitonal or blotted, look for a better 1929 copy before extracting.
items.pitch: Thirty-one letters Nehru wrote to ten-year-old Indira in 1928, telling the story of the earth, early peoples and civilisations.
